messages.author: d3cb5abb144524de
messages.subject: Skyline Report Template for MSstatsPTM
parts:
Hi all,

Is there a Skyline report template that exists for getting data out of Skyline in an appropriate format for the SkylinetoMSstatsPTMFormat converter?

At the moment I have been exporting a customized report and then re-formatting it with R as required. However, with an attempt of not trying to re-invent the wheel, I wanted to check if this had been standardized already.

The current MSstatsInput4 report that gets downloaded with the tool in Skyline is giving me an error when I run it through the converter:

Error in setnames(input, c("Protein Name", "Peptide Sequence", "Peptide Modified Sequence"), : Items of 'old' not found in column names: [Peptide Sequence]. Consider skip_absent=TRUE.

Attached is a subset of the exported report.
Sincerely,
Juan C.

messages.author: 13904eb0f06097b0
messages.subject: Re: Skyline Report Template for MSstatsPTM
parts:
Hi Juan,

Are you able to download the standard MSstats report format from Skyline? This converter was built assuming that format. We should just need the standard MSstats report with the `Peptide.Modified.Sequence` column. 

With that being said I have not seen too many Skyline PTM experiments so we may still need to tweak the converter a bit. Let me know!

Best,
Devon

messages.subject: Re: Skyline Report Template for MSstatsPTM
parts:
Hi Juan,

Apologies I have been out of the office the past week and hadn't had time to look into this until now.

This is actually an interesting problem that I haven't seen before. The problem is as below:

For protein sp|P02768|ALBU_HUMAN and modification at K543 there are two modified peptides reported by Skyline: 
TFHADICTLSEK[+312.1]ER
TFHADICTLSEK[+383.1]ER

Right now the converter is not handling these correctly and I was hoping you might be able to provide guidance on how you would like them to be handled.

The options are: 
1. Treat each peptide sequence as its own feature and use them both to summarize up to the modification level (e.g., with median summarization)
2. Treat them as a psuedo repeat measurements and use some pre-summarization method to handle them (taking the max or sum of each peptide)

I am not sure which of these options would be best, but can certainly implement which ever solution makes the most sense.

Devon

parts:
Hi Devon,

So this issue will be related to another entry in this Google Group:

https://groups.google.com/g/msstats/c/2ZqG4esluUc

This dataset has multiple instances of the scenario you showed and is why I inquired if it would be sensible to add modification specificity to the modification site evaluation. Some peptidoforms with up to 10 distinct versions, corresponding to derivatized versions of reactive electrophiles and amino acid side chain oxidation products.

I am inclined to go for option 1 as perhaps would be the most simple one assuming these PTMs are independent from each other. But I cannot discard that combinations of these might show similar regulation patterns.

That said, I am open to suggestions.

Let me know what else I can do to help.

Sincerely,
Juan C.

Hi Devon,

So this issue will be related to another entry in this Google Group:

https://groups.google.com/g/msstats/c/2ZqG4esluUc

This dataset has multiple instances of the scenario you showed and is why I inquired if it would be sensible to add modification specificity to the modification site evaluation. Some peptidoforms with up to 10 distinct versions, corresponding to derivatized versions of reactive electrophiles and amino acid side chain oxidation products.

I am inclined to go for option 1 as perhaps would be the most simple one assuming these PTMs are independent from each other. But I cannot discard that combinations of these might show similar regulation patterns.

That said, I am open to suggestions.

Let me know what else I can do to help.

On Tuesday, February 13, 2024 at 4:12:16 PM UTC+1 devonj...@gmail.com wrote:
Hi Juan,

Apologies I have been out of the office the past week and hadn't had time to look into this until now.

This is actually an interesting problem that I haven't seen before. The problem is as below:

For protein sp|P02768|ALBU_HUMAN and modification at K543 there are two modified peptides reported by Skyline: 
TFHADICTLSEK[+312.1]ER
TFHADICTLSEK[+383.1]ER

Right now the converter is not handling these correctly and I was hoping you might be able to provide guidance on how you would like them to be handled.

The options are: 
1. Treat each peptide sequence as its own feature and use them both to summarize up to the modification level (e.g., with median summarization)
2. Treat them as a psuedo repeat measurements and use some pre-summarization method to handle them (taking the max or sum of each peptide)

I am not sure which of these options would be best, but can certainly implement which ever solution makes the most sense.

Devon
